articles.title: Introducing The Back Room: India's First Pour-Only Cocktail Bar in Chandigarh, ETHospitalityWorld
articles.content: A city known for its architecture, design and thoughtful urban planning now welcomes a destination that speaks the same language of precision and intent: The Back Room , the newest venture from Saanya and Akshay Verma of VTC Group , opens its doors as India’s first pour-only cocktail bar at The Toy Hotel, Sector 34A, Chandigarh. Every planned city has a back room. This is Chandigarh’s. Conceived not only as a neighbourhood bar but as a destination worth travelling for, The Back Room is a concept that challenges every convention of how cocktails are made, served and experienced. Designed by French interior architect Jean-Louis Deniot and featuring a cocktail programme by Beverage Director Tanka Gurung, The Back Room offers an entirely new reason for guests to plan their journeys around, reserve well in advance and return to, not simply for a drink, but for moments that are unlike any other in the country. At the heart of the concept lies a radical commitment to consistency. Every cocktail begins its journey inside the lab, The Back Room’s dedicated bartenders’ workspace, where recipes are developed, tested and measured in grams rather than millilitres. Each drink is built, batched, rested and sealed in a large-format bottle before service, then poured at the table, so that every pour delivers exactly the same drink, every single time. The result is India’s first and only pour-only cocktail programme: no shaking, no stirring and no theatre behind the bar. Instead, the focus shifts entirely to the quality of the drink, the precision of its execution and the conversation around it. The menu itself pays homage to Chandigarh’s modernist planning. Cocktails are ordered not by name but by intuitive three-digit code, each digit representing a drink’s base spirit, method and flavour profile: a nod to the city’s numbered sectors and structured grid. Guests order by coordinate. The kitchen was built the other way around. Rather than bolting a food menu onto a bar, The Back Room designed its plates backwards from the glass: a concise, globally fluent tapas menu in which every dish is umami-forward, punchy enough to hold its own against spirits and sharp enough to improve the drink beside it. The brief was the house line in one sentence: the right punch and flavour, perfect with every spirit. Organised by temperature and technique, Fresh, Street, Fire and Slow & Smoky, with a short At the Bar card, Small Plates and Afters alongside, the menu travels freely: pani puri rebuilt as Mexican agua chile, jhol momos spiked with sambal or set afloat in tom kha, corn ribs crumbed in chilli coconut, prawns straight off the plancha, burrata with charred peppers. Everything is made to be shared. The menu is the work of Chef Megha Kohli and Noah Barnes of Logic Hospitality. At The Back Room, food is not the opening act. articles.title: 2 GRP Constables Suspended For Allegedly Facilitating Gutkha Transport Through Mumbai Trains
articles.content: 2 GRP Constables Suspended For Allegedly Facilitating Gutkha Transport Through Mumbai Trains Railway Police Commissioner Rakesh Kalasagar suspended two GRP constables, Anil Gujar and Tushar Thakur, over allegations that they facilitated gutkha transportation from Gujarat to Mumbai through trains. The action followed a citizen complaint and departmental inquiry. Authorities are examining claims that consignments were concealed in AC coaches and moved through long-distance trains. Add FPJ As a Trusted Source Megha Kuchik Updated: Sunday, September 13, 2026, 11:17 AM IST 2 GRP Constables Suspended For Allegedly Facilitating Gutkha Transport Through Mumbai Trains | AI Representational Image Mumbai: Railway Police Commissioner Rakesh Kalasagar has issued suspension orders against two Government Railway Police (GRP) constables for allegedly facilitating the transportation of gutkha from Gujarat to Mumbai in trains. The suspended personnel are Anil Gujar from Borivali GRP and Tushar Thakur of Vasai GRP. ALSO READ India’s First Vande Bharat Freight EMU Completes 130 Kmph Trial Run On Western Railway Network For... Inquiry into gutkha transport A departmental inquiry followed a citizen’s complaint alleging the constables were in contact with gutkha suppliers and helped transport consignments. Sources said the product was allegedly carried in AC coaches, concealed in storage compartments and among bedroll storage areas in black bags. Suppliers allegedly paid storage contractors, while certain Railway Protection Force and other personnel were allegedly paid to allow the consignments. Also Watch: Trains allegedly used The consignments were allegedly loaded at Vasai or Borivali and transported by taxis. Trains allegedly used included Suryanagari Express, Golden Temple Mail, Garib Rath Express, Awadh Express, Bhavnagar Express and Haridwar Express, with several long-distance trains arriving at Bandra Terminus. articles.title: CSIR-IMMT-led consortium to develop India's first 100 pc hydrogen DRI pilot plant - ThePrint
articles.content: Subscribe to Notifications Economy Kolkata, Sep 12 (PTI) The CSIR-Institute of Minerals and Materials Technology (CSIR-IMMT) will lead a Rs 207-crore national pilot project to develop India’s first direct reduced iron (DRI) plant running entirely on hydrogen, aimed at reducing carbon emissions from the steel sector, a senior official said. The 20-tonne-per-day pilot project has received in-principle approval from the Ministry of Steel and the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE). It will receive Rs 113 crore in government support under the National Green Hydrogen Mission, with the remaining funding to be contributed by consortium partners. CSIR-IMMT Director Ramanuj Narayan told PTI that the facility is expected to be completed by August 2029 and will focus on developing and demonstrating hydrogen-based DRI technology suited to Indian conditions, particularly the use of domestic iron ore. The consortium led by CSIR-IMMT includes Godavari Power and Ispat Ltd, Lloyd Steel, Jindal Stainless and Thyssenkrupp Industries India. Tata Steel has also agreed to join the consortium, and efforts are being made to bring other major steel producers, including Steel Authority of India Ltd (SAIL), into the project, said scientist P C Beuria, the head of the Mineral Processing Division at CSIR-IMMT. SP Das, chief scientist in the division, said some private steelmakers are currently working on projects involving partial use of hydrogen, with plans to increase its share gradually. “In contrast, the CSIR project is focusing on a 100 per cent hydrogen-based DRI plant,” he said. The proposed facility will use a vertical shaft furnace designed to operate entirely on hydrogen. Beuria said a key challenge will be processing India’s relatively low-grade hematite ores. Several international hydrogen-DRI projects use higher-grade magnetite, making the Indian raw material challenge different, he said. Das said Bhubaneswar-based CSIR-IMMT is working on ore processing and reduction technologies to ensure that the proposed plant can handle the characteristics of Indian iron ore. “Globally, the technology is still at the pilot stage, and the Indian challenge is different because of the inferior quality of ore available here,” he said. Beuria said the economics of green steel, however, remains a major hurdle. Green hydrogen currently costs around USD 5 per kg and would need to become substantially cheaper, at around USD 1 per kg, for hydrogen-based steelmaking to become commercially competitive. At present, green steel production costs around USD 200 more per tonne than conventional steel produced using fossil fuels, they said. To address the technological challenges involved in scaling up, CSIR-IMMT is undertaking intermediate-scale work before moving to the proposed national pilot plant. “The behaviour of materials changes when the process is scaled up, so intermediate-scale testing is important before moving to the 20-tonne-per-day facility,” Beuria said. As part of this effort, the institute is setting up a 3-tonne-per-day DRI plant using its own resources to bridge the gap between laboratory-scale experiments and the larger national pilot project. articles.title: Karnataka Police may shift to rental model for vehicles says Priyank Kharge
articles.content: Siddarth Sethia The Karnataka government is exploring the possibility of introducing a rental or leasing model for police vehicles as part of efforts to modernise the police department, reduce upfront capital expenditure and ensure quicker availability of vehicles for operational requirements. Home minister Priyank Kharge on Thursday held a meeting with officials from the Karnataka Police’s communications,logistics and modernisation wing and representatives of more than 20 automobile and two-wheeler manufacturers, including companies producing electric and conventional vehicles. The proposal seeks to provide an alternative to the existing practice of purchasing vehicles outright. Mr.Kharge said a rental or leasing model could enable the department to use its available resources more efficiently while responding quickly to changing operational requirements. “The government’s objective is not merely to purchase vehicles, but to use public money judiciously and improve the efficiency of the police department. Instead of making a large capital expenditure at one go, we will examine all possibilities of adding vehicles quickly according to the department’s requirements and managing their use and maintenance more efficiently,” Mr.Kharge said. Under the proposed model,the police could potentially increase its fleet according to operational needs and deploy vehicles for law and order duties,patrolling, emergency response and investigations.

articles.title: ToneTag launches India's first In-Car Fuel Payment solution
articles.content: Home Car News Car News Tata ToneTag launches India’s first In-Car Fuel Payment solution By Mohit Soni 13/09/2026 Follow Us On: Follow Us On: Vivek Kumar Singh, Co-founder and Director Labs, ToneTag, alongside dignitaries from IOCL, NPCI, and Tata Motors, at the official launch of DrivePay. ToneTag, a globalpayment infrastructure and sound-based communication technology company, has launched India’s first In-Car Fuel Payment solution at Global Fintech Fest (GFF) 2026, using an IoT-enabled implementation of NPCI’s UPI Circle framework for TATA.CARS’ DrivePay solutionin collaboration with IndianOil. The solution enables customers to securely pay for fuel at IndianOil outlets. DrivePay, powered by ToneTag, extends digital payments into connected vehicles, allowing customers to complete fuel payments through their vehicle’sinterface after refuelling, without using a separate mobile application, card or other payment method. Following its launch at GFF 2026, the solution is being deployed in collaboration with IndianOil to enable an In-Car Fuel Payment experience at IndianOilRetail Outlets, with a formal rollout expected in the coming months. The solution leverages NPCI’s UPI Circle framework, “Introduction of IoT Devices and Software on the UPI Ecosystem”, with ToneTag providing the technology layer that enables the IoT-based payment experience. By integrating the payment capability into the connected vehicle, DrivePay creates a secure, convenientand contactless way for customers to pay for fuel directly from their vehicle. Vivek Kumar Singh, Co-founder and Director Labs, ToneTag, alongside dignitaries from IOCL, NPCI, and Tata Motors, at the official launch of DrivePay. The solution will also integrate IndianOil’s XTRAREWARDS loyalty programme, enabling eligible customers to earn reward points without sharing theirmobile number during the transaction. The collaboration brings together IndianOil’s extensive fuel retail network, TATA.CARS’ connected vehicle ecosystem, ToneTag’s payment technology andNPCI’s digital payments infrastructure, creating a foundation for wider applications across in-vehicle payments, commerce and digital services. Following the successful implementation of DrivePay with TATA.CARS, ToneTag is not stopping here. The company sees a broader opportunity to extend its payment technologyacross the connected mobility ecosystem and will explore opportunities to work with other automotive OEMs and mobility ecosystem players to enable similar in-vehicle payment and commerce experiences. “Payments are rapidly moving beyond traditional interfaces such as cards and smartphones, and connected devices are emerging as the next frontierfor commerce. With DrivePay, powered by ToneTag, we are bringing an IoT-based UPI Circle payment experience directly into the connected vehicle. This initiative with IndianOil, TATA.CARS and NPCI demonstrates how payment infrastructure can seamlessly extendinto connected devices, enabling the vehicle itself to become a secure payment interface. We believe this is an important step towards a future where mobility, payments and commerce are seamlessly connected,” said Vivek Kumar Singh, Co-Founder and Director – Labs, ToneTag. With its connected car solution, ToneTag is bringing payments closer to where consumers interact with their vehicles, creating new possibilities forseamless and connected commerce experiences.
